So instead they try to chip away at things slowly under the guise of common sense.  In a certain state for example the gun laws suck. Religious traditions are passed down through word of mouth. The basic idea is someone says they heard a religious figure said or did something. The person they tell passes that along to someone else and so on and so on. Over generations. Then you get a 'chain' or link in the transmission. So you hear about something the religious figure did or said and you look back along the chain and see if the tradition is 'authentic' (true/trustworthy) or not. (There are several attributes that a chain can have that makes it 'weak' or unreliable. Like someone saying I heard from Bill who heard from bob who heard from Mary that the Prophet said "such and such". The chain would be weak if it was known that Mary had died before Bob was born, so Bob could not have heard what the Prophet said directly from Mary) As for who wrote them, there are 6 major written collections of these traditions. What is written is the words the religious figure said as well as each transmitter that makes up the chain. The top two recorders of these traditions are well-known scholars.

Our inventory was somewhat random. But for basic house/apartment furnishings you could find that pretty regularly. It rarely looks brand new (sometimes we got donations from furniture stores going out of business so the items were pristine) but if you need stuff for a decent price and don't mind some nicks, scratches or some mismatched items it's a good bet.  The money from the sale goes to funding builds of low income housing.  It is a religious based organization of that matters but the one I worked at was not bad. I was raised in a religious tradition but I am agnostic leaning towards atheist but never came up. The guy who ran it was religious but not a hardcore proselytizer or anything.  Each store is independent of each other so a store near you may not have similar stock or be run the same as the one I described above. But it's definitely worth checking out.
